newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QNI to form New Caledonia nickel jv.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QNI to form New Caledonia nickel jv.

text.p: Nickel producer QNI Ltd said on Thursday it plans to form a joint venture in the Pacific island of New Caledonia to explore and possibile develop nickel deposits.
QNI said it would form the venture with New Caledonian mining group, Noumea Entreprises SA, to start a joint exploration program of the BLM tenements in New Caledonia's southern province.

As part of the joint venture, QNI said it would buy 40 percent of Noumea Entreprises issued shares for A$730,000 through its unit QNI (Nouvelle-Caledonie S.A.). These funds would be spent on the BLM exploration program, it said.
"If the exploration results are favourable, approvals would be sought from the appropriate authorities to develop a mine," QNI said.
Managing director Wyn Davies said in a statement QNI was confident the exploration would identify quantities and grades of limonitic ore worthy of further development.

"Noumea Entreprises has been conducting low-key exploration on its 12 tenements on the south east corner of the southern province since the 1970s including some surface sampling, test pitting, drilling and mapping," Davies said.
"The BLM project offers a further opportunity for QNI to secure and diversify its ore supply," he said.
He said that the exploration programme was expected to be completed by mid-1997.

Davies said QNI was keen to continue its strong relationship with New Caledonia by investing in projects such as the Societe Des Mines De Bogota (SMB) project in the northern province and now the BLM project in the southern province of New Caledonia.
At 3.55 p.m. (0555 GMT), QNI shares were two cents up at A$2.48.
